summary: Ephemeral proxy rate jitter causing elevated 5xx floor on many small-payload requests
description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral proxy nodes in the us-east-1 ingress fleet exhibited rate jitter under a small-payload, high-QPS tenant workload causing a sustained elevation in 5xx error-rate across the tenant's requests (~2% -> 12%).

Impact:
- BrightForms (dedicated) observed widespread 5xx responses for short/fast embedding and chat calls between 11:20-12:40 UTC on 2026-03-12.
- Affected surface: REST generation and streaming endpoints for small payload requests (<200 bytes).
- Business impact: degraded UX and retries from the customer leading to amplified load.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east-1 region, dedicated capacity pool for BrightForms.
- Ingress path: api-gateway -> ephemeral-proxy -> runtime pool (dedicated GPU nodes).
- Autoscaling and prefetch enabled for the customer's model variants.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send ~3000 small POSTs/min (100-200B payload) across multiple connections with short TTL keepalives.
2) Ephemeral proxy acceptor queues occasionally backpressured (spiky accept latency) causing upstream hedged-retry logic to fire.
3) Hedged retries combined with apigw backoff mis-calibration produced request duplication leading to transient runtime overload and 5xx responses.

Logs/metrics snippets collected:
- apigw.ingress.accept_latency.p90: spiked from 8ms -> 120ms at 11:25 UTC.
- ephemeral-proxy.retry_count: +250% correlated with windowed accept latency spikes.
- runtime.request_5xx.rate: baseline 2% -> sustained 10-14% during peak.
- Sample error from runtime: "upstream-cancellation: capacity-exceeded"
- Kernel traces on runtime nodes showed increased context-switches and io wait during the spike.

Initial customer report:
- BrightForms sent a support email at 11:30 UTC reporting intermittent 500s during embedding uploads and chat completions at high QPS.

Observed differences vs a classic prefetch-thrash:
- This incident did not coincide with a model sync or prefetch invalidation window.
- Root cause appeared upstream in the ingress/ephemeral proxy path where jitter and hedged retry interactions amplified load rather than a pure runtime OOM or NVMe hotspot.
investigation_notes:
Timeline of investigation:
- 11:35 Support acknowledged and opened ticket; routed to SRE on-call.
- 11:45 SRE identified correlated spikes in ephemeral-proxy.retry_count and apigw.accept_latency.
- 11:55 Confirmed hedged-retry policy triggers under accept latency >50ms; found a recent canary tweak to hedged-retry backoff on 2026-03-11 (PR 119) that shortened the secondary retry window.
- 12:05 Replica set of ephemeral proxies in front of BrightForms showed uneven connection distribution (50% of connections funneled into 3 pods due to a transient routing hash change).
- 12:20 Implemented temporary mitigation: disabled hedged-retry for this tenant at apigw edge and increased accept queue size on affected ephemeral-proxy pods.
- 12:35 Error-rate began to fall; by 12:50 rates returned to baseline.
Hypotheses tested and results:
- Hypothesis A: Runtime OOMs caused 5xx -> disproved (no OOM/panic logs, memory stable).
- Hypothesis B: Prefetch invalidation caused thrash -> disproved (no prefetch sweeps in logs).
- Hypothesis C: Hedged retry + acceptor jitter amplified requests -> supported by correlated metrics and timeline.
Evidence and artifacts:
- Ingress routing logs showing connection-affinity shift at 11:22 UTC (investigation trace id: trace-20260312-1122).
- apigw and proxy traces (link to internal cycle-storage): /mnt/logs/ingress/2026-03-12/trace-1122.gz
- Heap and kernel traces on runtimes: /mnt/diag/runtime/brightforms/2026-03-12/
resolution:
Short-term actions applied (12:20-12:50 UTC):
- Disabled hedged-retry behavior for BrightForms at apigw gateway until hedged policy is tuned.
- Increased ephemeral-proxy accept queue depth on affected pods (nodes auto-healed/restarted to pick config).
- Applied routing fix to rebalance connections across ephemeral proxies (removed stale route-hash canary).

Long-term fix and follow-ups:
- Reverted the hedged-retry canary change in proxy (PR 119 rolled back) and opened follow-up PR 482 in gateway to add jitter and exponential backoff to hedged-retry.
- Add an admission check so connection hashing changes require a gradual drain window (Confluence: acceptor-queue-tuning-playbook).
- Update playbook to include a knob to disable hedged-retry per-tenant and automated detection alert when retry_count grows >100% within 5min.
- Run a targeted load test (small-payload high-QPS) with new hedged-retry settings before re-enabling.

Resolution notes:
- Ticket resolved after error rate returned to baseline and BrightForms confirmed acceptable behavior at 13:10 UTC.
- Post-incident monitoring window scheduled for 72 hours.
